issue_title: Local harness doesn't have all tools available when sending first message in new chat in Agents Window
issue_doc:
Local harness doesn't have all tools available when sending first message in new chat in Agents Window

Visual Studio Code - Insiders

ElectronBuildId: 14760073

1. Open the Agents Window.
2. Select the "Local" harness.
3. Observe that the tool picker (sliders icon) is missing from the new-chat composer (`NewChatInputWidget`).
4. Send a first message that requires tools or asks the model to list all available tools.
5. Observe that the model responds with only a restricted subset of tools (or none at all) because `ChatSelectedTools` was not initialized for the initial request.
6. Send a second message or resend the first message (which now utilizes the active session's `ChatInputPart` and `MenuId.ChatInput`).
7. Observe that all tools are now properly loaded and available.

Additional Context / Proposed Root Cause:
- The new-chat composer in the Agents Window uses `NewChatInputWidget`, which renders `Menus.NewSessionConfig` rather than `MenuId.ChatInput`. Consequently, `ConfigureToolsAction` (the tool-picker slider) never renders on turn one.
- `ChatSelectedTools` is not initialized for the new-chat state, resulting in an empty/omitted `enabledTools` payload on the initial request.

On a personal note, this makes the Agents Window very frustrating to use in an enterprise environment where the Local harness is the only one available. I have to remember to double-send messages when I open a new chat if I want Copilot to be effective / have all of the expected tools available to it. Here's a screenshot of my experience by asking the model to return back to me the tools that are available to it:

issue_title: gitCommitMessageGenerator Consistently Fails and Returns Error 422
issue_doc:
gitCommitMessageGenerator Consistently Fails and Returns Error 422

Environment

GitHub Copilot Chat extension: 0.56.0
VS Code: 1.128.0

Copilot token SKU: free_educational_quota
Model used for feature: gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18
Feature: gitCommitMessageGenerator (Source Control "Generate Commit Message" button)
Summary
Clicking "Generate Commit Message" in the Source Control panel fails 100% of the time with a 422 Unprocessable Entity from the Copilot backend. Started suddenly a few days ago with no local configuration changes. The personal account setting "Copilot-generated commit messages" is confirmed Enabled at github.com/settings/copilot.

Sign in to VS Code with a GitHub account on the free_educational_quota Copilot SKU.
Open any git repo with at least one uncommitted change (reproduced both in an existing project and in a brand-new blank repo with a single test file — rules out repo/org content-exclusion policy).
Open Source Control panel, click the "Generate Commit Message" sparkle button.
Request fails immediately; no commit message is generated.
Expected behavior
A commit message is generated from the staged/unstaged diff.

Actual behavior
Every request fails with a 422. Relevant log lines from GitHub Copilot Chat output channel:

[error] Server error: 422 Unprocessable Entity
ccreq:.copilotmd | promptFiltered | gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 | ~600-1000ms | [gitCommitMessageGenerator]
Every failed request is tagged promptFiltered alongside the 422, suggesting the request is being rejected by a content filter or SKU-entitlement check on the backend before generation completes, rather than a genuine client-side prompt issue.

Additional notes

Confirmed not repo-specific: reproduces identically in a throwaway blank local repo unrelated to any GitHub org.
Confirmed not an entitlement UI issue: github.com/settings/copilot shows "Copilot-generated commit messages" as Enabled.
Suspect this is tied to backend handling of the free_educational_quota SKU against the gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 model specifically for this feature.

picked_title: Voice mode: holding push-to-talk keybinding rapidly toggles instead of hold-to-talk
picked_doc:
Voice mode: holding push-to-talk keybinding rapidly toggles instead of hold-to-talk

### Describe the bug

In voice mode, holding down the push-to-talk keybinding (`Ctrl+Shift+Space`) in the chat input behaves erratically instead of acting as push-to-talk.

**Expected:** Pressing and holding the keybinding should enter listening mode, and releasing the key should stop recording and send the request.

**Actual:** Holding the key rapidly toggles recording on and off ("weird things").

### Root cause

The chat-input voice actions (`agentsVoice.startVoiceInChat` and `agentsVoice.pttStopInChat`) called `voiceController.pttDown()` and `voiceController.pttUp()` synchronously, back-to-back:

Because `pttUp()` fires within ~0ms — below the controller's tap threshold (`_PTT_TOGGLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 300`) — the controller always interprets it as a *tap* and enters toggle mode, never true hold-to-talk. Worse, while the key is held, the OS emits keyboard auto-repeat `keydown` events, which re-dispatch the command repeatedly. Each repeat flips between `pttDown` (start listening), toggle, and finish/send, producing rapid start/stop cycling.

### Fix

Use `IKeybindingService.enableKeybindingHoldMode(
judge_evidence: Both reports describe voice/dictation/push-to-talk getting stuck and not stopping when canceled; candidate #322395 specifically covers voice mode hold-to-talk/stop behavior going wrong, which matches the unresponsive dictation cancellation.

picked_title: Agents window: model/agent selection is shared across chats in a session instead of per chat
picked_doc:
Agents window: model/agent selection is shared across chats in a session instead of per chat

## Describe the bug

In the Agents window, a single session can contain multiple peer chats (tabs). Changing the **agent** or **model** in one chat also changes it in the other chats of the same session. These decisions should be scoped per chat.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Agents window and start an agent-host session that supports multiple chats.
2. Add a second chat to the session (so the session has 2+ chat tabs).
3. In chat A, change the model (or the agent).
4. Switch to chat B.

**Expected:** Chat B keeps its own model/agent selection, independent of chat A.
**Actual:** The model/agent picker reflects (and is driven by) a single shared selection, so changing it in one chat appears to change it in the others.

## Root cause

The provider's write path (`setModel`/`setAgent`) already targets the active chat's resource, and each `IChat` carries its own `modelId`/`mode` observables. However, `VisibleSession` (the `IActiveSession` implementation that the Agents window model/agent pickers bind to) exposed the **session/default chat's** `modelId`/`mode` rather than the active chat's
judge_evidence: Both reports describe an Agents/Agent Host session where the model selection is not retained per chat and switching between chats causes the UI to revert/change to another model. Candidate #323743 specifically says model selection is shared across chats in a session instead of per chat, matching the described model switching back when returning to the first chat.

TPI) Agent Host Copilot terminal output streaming

Refs: #324825, #327067

- [x] macOS @bryanchen-d 
- [x] linux @deepak1556 
- [x] windows @jruales 

Complexity: 4

---

Verify that Agent Host Copilot streams output from the Copilot SDK built-in shell tool live in the chat terminal UI.

Prerequisites:
- Use the latest VS Code Insiders
- Sign in to GitHub Copilot
- Enable `chat.agentHost.enabled`
- Set `chat.agentHost.customTerminalTool.enabled` to `false` so Agent Host uses the Copilot SDK built-in shell tool

Part 1: Command output
- Start an Agent Host Copilot session
- Ask the agent: "Run something that prints a random number every second for the next 20 seconds"
- The agent can use a command such as:
 
- Confirm each numbered result appears progressively while the command is running instead of all output appearing after completion
- Confirm the terminal UI automatically expands while new output is arriving
- Confirm the command changes from running to completed when it finishes

Part 2: Successful and failing commands
- Run a command that succeeds and confirm its completed state reflects a successful exit
- Run a command that exits with a non-zero status and confirm its completed state reflects the failure
- Confirm the final output remains visible and readable after both commands complete

Part 3: Output integrity
- Run commands that produce:
 - multiple output lines
 - enough output to exercise retained or truncated output
- Confirm output is not duplicated, reordered, stale, or missing
- Confirm output from one shell call does not appear in another shell call
- Confirm the final completed output is consistent with what was shown while the command was running

Part 4: Completed output and session history
- Run several terminal commands in the same Agent Host Copilot session
- Collapse and expand completed shell calls and confirm their output is preserved
- Reload the window or resume the session and confirm completed shell output is restored correctly
- Confirm completed output does not create an additional terminal in the Terminal panel

Part 5: Exploratory
- Use the built-in shell naturally during an Agent Host Copilot coding session
- Try commands that produce ongoing output, such as builds, tests, and `npm install`
- Note any cases where:
 - output does not appear until the command completes
 - output is duplicated, stale, reordered, or missing
 - a completed command continues to appear as running
 - completed output disappears after reload or r

issue_title: Built-in skills are not returned by the sessionless commands.list API (skills unavailable in sessionless chat input completions)
issue_doc:
Built-in skills are not returned by the sessionless commands.list API (skills unavailable in sessionless chat input completions)

## Summary

The sessionless `commands.list()` API does not return built-in skills. As a result, skills are **not available in the sessionless chat input completions** — they only become available **after a session has been created**.

## Details

- The sessionless `commands.list()` API filters returned commands to those flagged `availableAtSessionStart`.
- Skills are always `availableAtSessionStart: false`, so **no skills appear in that RPC at all** (including built-in skills bundled with the runtime).
- Skills are instead surfaced through a separate API surface — `skills.discover` / `session.skills.list()` and the `session.skills_loaded` event — all of which require (or are tied to) a loaded session.

## Impact

- When a user has not yet created a session (i.e. the sessionless chat input), skill slash commands do not show up in input completions.
- Built-in skills in particular are effectively invisible until a session exists, which is surprising because they ship with the runtime and could reasonably be offered at session start.
- This creates an inconsistent completion experience: built-in commands (e.g. runtime commands) are completable pre-session, but skills are not.

## Expected

Skills (at minimum built-in skills) should be discoverable/completable in the sessionless chat input, or there should be a documented, intentional reason why skill completions require a session.

## Notes

The implementing repository is private, so this issue captures the behavior at a conceptual level rather than linking source. Happy to provide more detail on request.
picked_title: Agent Host: runtime slash commands (e.g. /chronicle) don't autocomplete in the new-session composer
picked_doc:
Agent Host: runtime slash commands (e.g. /chronicle) don't autocomplete in the new-session composer

## Problem

In an Agent Host Copilot (`copilotcli`) session, runtime slash commands do **not** autocomplete in the **new-session composer** (the "New session in … with Copilot" input, before a session has been created). Typing `/chro` there shows no `/chronicle` suggestion. Once the session is live (after the first message / session creation), the same input correctly autocompletes `/chronicle` and other runtime commands.

This is **not** specific to `/chronicle` — **no** runtime slash command appears in the pre-creation composer, because runtime commands are only discoverable through a live SDK session.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the Agent Host (`node ./scripts/code-agent-host.js`).
2. Open the **new-session composer** ("New session in with Copilot"), provider = Copilot.
3. Type `/chro` (or just `/`).
4. Observe: no runtime slash-command completions (`/chronicle`, etc.). Only completions that don't require a live session (skills/files) may appear.
5. Create/start the session (send a first message), then type `/chro` again.
6. Observe: `/chronicle` (and its subcommand options)
judge_evidence: Both describe a sessionless/new-session composer autocomplete gap where slash commands/skills are unavailable until a live session exists. Candidate #324645 specifically says runtime slash commands don't autocomplete in the new-session composer before session creation, matching the same underlying bug about pre-session discoverability.

issue_title: Single Panel Detail Panel: File keeps closing
issue_doc:
Single Panel Detail Panel: File keeps closing

I've been using `singlePaneDetailPanel` for a bit now, and while I like the overall structure and approach, there are some issues that frustrated my experience. I imagine some are just small bugs in the preview, others maybe tweaks.

### 1 - Files keeps being closed
I want to quickly switch to files, check things, then revert to changes, and so on. Problem is: Files keeps closing. The reason is that "Files" switches to the individual file once I select it, so when I close, the Files tab is gone. While I can see the logic that "well it's opening one file", the fact the window is presented with the tree view on the side, it's effective how one would also browse files.

Steps:
1. Open the "Files" tab
2. Select one file
3. I'm done, close the file
4. Outcome: the files tree is now gone, and I've to re-add it as a tab.

An idea: barred larger flow fixes, one idea would simply be that if the file is pinned, when closed, it restores the empty "Files" selector instead of closing the tab.

### 2 - Changes show just one file
I appreciate the view with the full list of changes as a single list. For some things it's great. But when I want to see only one file, I keep accidentally scrolling too far in either direction, which is frustrating.

Steps:
1. Open the "Changes" view
2. Click on one specific file in the tree/list view
3. Outcome: scrolls to a file

An idea: provide a way to switch from a single list of all changes, to changes one-file-at-time so it can't scroll away (similar to how collapse all / expand all happens). Having a quick toggle like that would help switching view easily depending on the need / task.
